surface: Links autoLink draws in cells: a URL beside an opted-out one, a link inside a sentence, an email link, a HYPERLINK formula's label, and opening a link with Alt+Enter.

steps.note: B1 holds a URL in a column that opts out of autoLink (`autoLink: false`): plain text, no link. A group cannot require an absence, so the goldens show whether a reader says `link` here (none does). The groups ask for one word of each URL (`optout`, `one`, `someone`), because NVDA spells the punctuation of a URL (`example dot com slash one`). Finding: VoiceOver says nothing on this first arrow key, on both browsers.

A1 holds `https://example.com/one`, which autoLink wraps in a link: the cell's text and the link role. Column D's custom link reads `user anchor`, not a text with the word link: VoiceOver with Chromium reads the whole row with a cell, so that text would satisfy the link group on its own. Finding: NVDA reads the URL but never says `link`, on both browsers and on every link step: the focus stays on the cell, whose name is its text, and the link inside it (tabindex -1) never takes the focus. VoiceOver says `link` on every link step.

A2 holds a sentence with a URL in the middle, `Visit https://example.com/two for details.`: the text around the link and the link role. Finding: NVDA says no `link`, as in arrow-left-link; VoiceOver says it after the URL.

A3 holds `mailto:someone@example.com`. The grid hides the `mailto:` prefix, and every reader reads the link as the address (`someone at example dot com`). Finding: NVDA says no `link`, as in arrow-left-link.
F1 holds `=HYPERLINK("https://example.com/hf", "HF label")`: a link whose name is its label, not its URL. Finding: NVDA says no `link`, as in arrow-left-link.
A7 holds a link to a page of the same server (`/tests/fixtures/demo/grid.html`), which the next step opens, so the run stays offline. Finding: NVDA says no `link`, as in arrow-left-link.

Alt+Enter opens the selected cell's first link in a new tab (autoLink's default target, `_blank`). Every reader follows the new tab and reads its title, `Handsontable e2e fixture`; NVDA spells `e2e` as `e 2e`, the same title in its words. The last step, because the focus stays on the new tab; the test's browser context closes it.
